title: Resilient streaming backpressure: cleanup for client disconnects, timeouts, and partial outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce incomplete/duplicate output and resource leakage when a client disconnects or a request times out while streaming token-by-token. Ensure partial generations are logged, traceable, and either reconciled or safely discarded depending on API compatibility rules (structured outputs, function/tool calls).
acceptance_criteria: Server stops ongoing generation within SLO (<=500ms) after detecting client TCP/HTTP disconnect or explicit stream abort
Partial outputs are marked in logs/traces with a consistent reason code (CLIENT_DISCONNECT | TIMEOUT | SERVER_PREEMPT) and linked to request id
No orphaned GPU work or KV cache state remains for >30s after a disconnect under normal load
When structured output mode is enabled, partial JSON fragments are rejected upstream and a stable error wrapper is returned to callers or to tool invocations as per compatibility policy
Function/tool-calling flows that receive early disconnects either roll back side effects (when possible) or emit compensating events to the observability stream
Automated tests cover simulated disconnects, client-side cancellations, and long-tail timeouts across hosted/dedicated/private deployments
technical_notes: Current runtime cancels generation but KV cache entries and in-flight CUDA kernels sometimes remain scheduled until op completion. We need a two-phase teardown: (1) soft-cancel that signals model loop to stop token emission ASAP, (2) forced preemption path that halts kernel queues and clears per-request allocations. Also add an internal 'streaming_state' lifecycle with well-defined transitions and reason codes to make metrics and audits reliable. For function calls, we must integrate with the tool-execution coordinator to surface partial-call outcomes and to support idempotency hooks.
implementation_plan: Add StreamingState enum and lifecycle transitions in runtime-core (OPEN -> CANCELLING -> CANCELLED -> CLEANED)
Implement soft-cancel signal in generation loop that sets a per-request abort flag and stops batching new tokens
Introduce forced preempt API to kernel scheduler to evict/terminate queued ops tied to request id
Instrument KV cache to record last-access timestamp and request ownership to allow aggressive eviction of canceled requests
Extend observability: emit streaming_teardown event with reason code, elapsed tokens, partial_output_hash
Wire runtime teardown into function/tool-call coordinator so tool processes receive explicit CANCELLED signal and can run compensating logic
test_plan: Unit: streaming_state transitions and reason codes
Integration: simulated HTTP client disconnects at various token offsets and assert server teardown within budget
Load: interrupt 1% of streams under sustained 2k rps to validate no memory/GPU accumulation for 30min
Compatibility: verify structured-output endpoints return stable error wrapper for partial JSON and do not pass fragments to downstream processors
Chaos: kill long-lived worker process during streaming and assert auto-recovery and metrics emission
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 5% of hosted traffic and one dedicated cluster for 48h
Monitor: streaming_teardown rate, cancelled_vs_completed ratio, orphaned_gpu_ops gauge
Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if no regressions
Backout: disable feature flag and revert scheduler preempt changes if orphaned ops or latency regressions >5%
